glass.summary:
This is the full spec for glass in Cycles 5.1.2 and for fitting it into the ReSTIR PT hybrid shift. Sources: the in-app Cycles kernel, v5.1.2 host code (`shader.tables`, `cycles_precompute`, `shader.cpp`), the glTF and USD importers, and headless Blender introspection. Every formula was checked with a numpy port of Cycles' GGX glass closure. That port reproduces `table_ggx_glass_E` to Monte Carlo precision, which confirms that Cycles applies no 1/η² radiance scaling.

**The glass closure.**
- Principled Transmission, the Glass node and the Refraction node all use one GGX glass/refraction closure (Walter 2007 form).
- Fresnel is the real dielectric Fresnel, remapped to [f0, 1].
- Reflection vs refraction is chosen per sampled microfacet with probability P_R = avg(R)/avg(R+T). Under total internal reflection (TIR) T = 0.
- Principled tints transmission by sqrt(min(BaseColor,1)) at each interface. The Glass node tints both reflection and transmission by Color.
- η flips to 1/ior on backfacing hits and is decided locally at each hit. There is no thin-walled mode and no Transmission Roughness input.
- Glass is opaque to all shadow rays.

**Behind glass.** Through smooth (delta) glass, a floor gets exactly zero light from analytic lights in mode A and from delta lights in every mode. Through rough glass, light arrives only via NEE from the inner (exit) surface. With MIS on (mode B), area lights reach the floor through smooth glass only as BSDF-sampled caustics. So the plan's claim that Mode A and Mode B have identical expectation is false whenever a delta lobe sits just before the light. The same holds for mirrors.

**A spurious region in Cycles' refraction eval.** `eval` never checks whether the refraction half-vector configuration is valid (there is a TODO in the source). It returns nonzero eval and pdf for directions the sampler can never produce; its pdf integrates to 1.11–1.92 at high roughness. The fix, called support-consistent MIS:
- NEE keeps Cycles' eval exactly.
- Every pdf used for MIS, footprints, Jacobians and χ² tests is the true sampler density.
- Shifted BSDF-sampled segments carry a sampler-support indicator.

This keeps our ReSTIR and our PT equal for any heuristic and any RIS-NEE M. It is exact against Cycles in mode A and for emitters set to emission_sampling='NONE'.

**ReSTIR integration.**
- One new lobe class G; lobe codes grow to 3 bits.
- Delta is decided per sub-event: T is also delta when |η−1| < 1e-4.
- Rough glass can take either role in a reconnection pair (x_{k−1} or x_k); delta glass can take neither.
- Random replay through any glass is the identity with J = 1, so TIR never makes the shift undefined.
- Jacobians contain no η² factor.
- Each bounce uses 4 RNG dimensions.

**Validation.** New closed-form scenes are a smooth slab in a furnace, E = F + (1−F)·C·(1−F^N), and an emitter inside glass, E = (1−F)·√C·L_e. The report also gives semi-analytic rough-glass scenes, parity scenes, planted-bias controls and glTF/USD import mappings. The report is written to the plan-file path because plan mode was active.
key_facts: [SOURCE svm/closure.h:98-509] Principled builds closures in this order, starting from weight = mix_weight·alpha: metal m·weight, then weight *= (1−m); glass t·weight, then weight *= (1−t) (no albedo layering after the glass); IOR-level η'; dielectric specular (1−t)(1−m); diffuse C·(1−t)(1−m)·Λ_S(μ).

[SOURCE closure.h:378-411] The Principled glass closure uses N = valid_reflection_N and isotropic α = r² (anisotropy is ignored). η_side = backfacing ? 1/ior : ior, using the node IOR, not η'. f0 = saturate(F0(ior)·SpecularTint), f90 = 1, exponent −ior (real Fresnel remapped). reflection_tint = 1; transmission_tint = sqrt(min(BaseColor,1)) per interface.

[SOURCE closure.h:779-832] The Glass node's closure weight is mix_weight (grey); Color goes into both the reflection and the transmission tint, and f0 = F0(ior). The Refraction node has Fresnel NONE: R = 0 and T = 1 except under TIR (T = 0, energy lost); its weight is Color.

[VERIFIED BPY] Glass node distribution defaults to MULTI_GGX (enum BECKMANN/GGX/MULTI_GGX); Refraction node defaults to BECKMANN (enum BECKMANN/GGX); Principled defaults to MULTI_GGX. Principled 5.1.2 has no 'Transmission Roughness' input. Thin Film Thickness defaults to 0 and Thin Film IOR to 1.33. Bounce defaults are max 12, diffuse 4, glossy 4, transmission 12, volume 0, transparent 8. MNEE flags (object is_caustics_caster/receiver, light is_caustics_light) default to False.

[SOURCE bsdf_microfacet.h:586-675] Refraction eval: H = −(η·L + V)/|·|; common = D/cNI · (η/|V+ηL|)²·|cHI·(H·L)| (the half-vector Jacobian η²|o·h|/(i·h+η o·h)²); pdf = common·(1−P_R)/(1+Λ_I); eval·cos = T·common/(1+Λ_I+Λ_O). Reflection uses common = D/(4cNI). P_R = avg(R)/avg(R+T) at the evaluated H.

[SOURCE bsdf_microfacet.h:677-820] Sampling: H from VNDF (H = N if α² ≤ 2e-10); refract iff u.z ≥ P_R(H·V); the sample is rejected unless sign(Ng·L) and sign(N·L) match the event. Refraction is also singular when |η−1| < 1e-4. A singular sample returns eval·1e6 and pdf·1e6, so its weight is T/(1−P_R) or R/P_R, and it sets PATH_RAY_MIS_SKIP. Cycles reuses the rescaled closure-pick random number as u.z.

[VERIFIED NUM] There is no η² radiance scaling: bsdf_eta is used only for path guiding. The refraction weight is T/P_T·G2/G1. Our port's single-scatter albedo matches table_ggx_glass_E, e.g. MC 0.98866 vs table 0.98860 at r=0.533, μ=1, η=1.557. The T part is 0.946, not the 0.39 that η² scaling would give.

[VERIFIED NUM + SOURCE TODO bsdf_microfacet.h:621-623] Cycles' refraction eval never checks the validity of the generalized half-vector. The integrated eval pdf is 1.1126 at r=0.533, μ=0.4, η=1.557 and 1.9213 at r=1, μ=0.2. The eval energy the sampler can never produce is 0.106 and 0.60 respectively; it is 0.0011 at r=0.2. Valid-only integrals equal the sampler's MC albedo.
[VERIFIED] F_gs equals the real dielectric Fresnel for 1/3.73 < η_side < 3.73 on both sides (white Specular Tint). It clips at η = 3.8 (−1.6e-4) and η = 4 (−2.2e-3).

[SOURCE intersect_filter.h:151-160, shade_shadow.h:60-66, surface_shader.h:948-957, CYH shader.cpp:628-640] Shadow rays are blocked unless the shader has SD_HAS_TRANSPARENT_SHADOW (Transparent BSDF, Ray Portal, Principled with Alpha < 1 or linked, or any volume). Even then the transmitted fraction is the transparent closure weight, which is 0 for glass. Glass always blocks NEE, including glass with a volume.

[SOURCE light.h:283-286] Non-camera rays skip lights without SHADER_USE_MIS, even after singular bounces. So in mode A, smooth glass and mirrors never transmit or reflect analytic-light radiance, while mode B does so through BSDF-sampled caustics. Mode A equals Mode B only when no light-ending path has a delta lobe at x_{d−1}.

[INFERENCE, derived from source] What Cycles renders for a point light, or a mode-A area light, behind a smooth pane over a diffuse floor: exactly 0 in the pane's shadow. Behind a rough closed slab: nonzero via floor→entry face (BSDF refraction)→exit face (NEE through the transmission lobe, weight 1); this needs max_bounces ≥ 2. Behind a rough single-quad pane: NEE straight through the pane. A mode-B area light behind smooth glass: a BSDF-only caustic with weight 1 after the singular bounces.

[SOURCE triangle.h:30-43, shader_data.h:107-113] Ng = normalize(cross(v1−v0, v2−v0)), reversed for objects with negative scale applied. Backfacing (Ng·V < 0) flips N and Ng and makes the glass η = 1/ior. There is no medium stack and no nested-dielectric logic.
[SOURCE path_state.h:110-231] Each glass transmission increments both bounce and transmission_bounce; reflection off glass counts as a glossy bounce. max_bounces counts every glass interface.

[SOURCE bsdf_microfacet.h:423-499] The glass lobe's sample weight is |avg(w)|·avg(mix(f0,1,lut3(r,μ,z,gen_schlick_ior_s))·rt + (1−F_gs(N·V))·tt). It is noise-only. Example: grey C=0.8, IOR 1.5, r=0.5, t=0.5, μ=1 gives q(G) = 0.5267, q(S) = 0.0237, q(D) = 0.4496.

[VERIFIED checksums] The Tier-2 glass tables are table_ggx_glass_E[4096] (Σ 3758.664856), glass_Eavg[256] (Σ 235.910746), glass_inv_E[4096] (Σ 3477.751955) and glass_inv_Eavg[256] (Σ 216.090299). Their multiplier 1/E ranges from ×1.008–1.057 (front, r=0.5) up to ×2.37 (inside, r=1, μ=1).

[VERIFIED NUM; cause UNVERIFIED] In the TIR regime, glass_inv_E does not match the 5.1.2 sampler's albedo: table 0.8041 vs MC 0.7893, and table 0.5649 vs MC 0.5060. Tier 2 must port the tables verbatim.

[VERIFIED against an MC emulation of Cycles' sampling] Smooth-slab furnace closed form: Principled gives E = F + (1−F)·C·(1−F^N) and the Glass node gives E = cF + c²(1−F)²(1−(cF)^N)/(1−cF). Example: θ=80°, C=1, N=1: MC 0.76299 vs formula 0.76261.

[SOURCE GLTF pbrMetallicRoughness.py] The glTF importer maps Transmission Weight = transmissionFactor × texture R channel. IOR comes from KHR_materials_ior, else 1.5. Volume Absorption is created only if thicknessFactor ≠ 0, with Color = attenuationColor and Density = 1/attenuationDistance, so Cycles uses σ_a = (1−color)·density rather than glTF's −ln(c)/d. distribution is not set, so it stays MULTI_GGX. There is no thin-walled mode.

[SOURCE USD usd_reader_material.cc:614-642] Blender's USD importer maps UsdPreviewSurface opacity to Transmission Weight = 1 − opacity (glass) when opacityThreshold == 0 and opacity is not connected to a texture's alpha. Otherwise it maps to Alpha.
design_recommendations: Add one lobe class G (Cycles' GGX glass/refraction closure; reflect vs refract follows from sign(N·L)). Widen lobe codes to 3 bits: D=0, S=1, G=2, TRANSP=3 (reserved), NEE=4, NONE=5. Add side bits for x_{k−1} and x_k (bits 28–29). Keep S separate from G.

Adopt support-consistent MIS as a normative rule. NEE uses Cycles' eval unchanged, spurious part included. p2 in NEE/emitter MIS, p̄ in footprints, joint pdfs in Jacobians and the χ² tests all use the valid-only sampler density. Every shifted BSDF-sampled segment (ω' at y_{k−1}, ω_k at x_k) is multiplied by the sampler-support indicator, including the refraction half-vector validity test.

Implement f_G exactly as Cycles does, with no 1/η² radiance scaling, in the PT, initial sampling and every shift re-evaluation. Jacobians have no η² term; η enters only through the evaluated pdfs. Compute η_side from local backfacing (Ng·V computed from reconstructed positions, same formula in base and replay). Glass occludes every visibility query. Do not port Falcor's nested-dielectric or LDeltaDirect logic.

Make delta per sub-event. Reflection is delta iff α² ≤ 2e-10. Transmission is delta iff α² ≤ 2e-10 or |η_side−1| < 1e-4. D_k and R_k use r_G (the perceptual Roughness input). G is never 'diffuse-only', so the inverse footprint is always evaluated.

Random replay through glass (R/T switch, TIR, change of lobe class) is the PSS identity with J = 1. TIR at a reconnection half-vector gives f = 0, not an undefined shift. Offer an optional, symmetric 'same side at y_{k−1}' restriction as an experiment flag, off by default.
Use 4 RNG dimensions per bounce: (u_lobe, u_h1, u_h2, u_rt), fixed for every material.
Fix gap-bsdf §11 ggx_lambda to use max(abs(cosN), 1e-7). As written, it zeroes G2 for every transmission. Add regression test U-G10.

In cycles_settings.py / build_scene.py, force distribution='GGX' on Principled, Glass (default MULTI_GGX) and Refraction (default BECKMANN) nodes. Assert MNEE is off. Support emission_sampling='NONE' per material in both renderers: excluded from the alias table, forward-hit MIS weight 1.

Rough-glass validation must use only mode-A analytic lights and/or emissive meshes with emission_sampling='NONE'. Mode B plus rough-glass NEE through the exit surface goes into a separate approximate-parity tolerance tier.

Correct the plan's 'Mode A ≡ Mode B' claim: it holds only when no light-ending path has a delta lobe at x_{d−1}. Restrict the invariance test to scenes without singular BSDFs, and add negative control G6-neg. Consider Mode B for area lights in the interactive app when glass or mirrors are present.

Add validation scenes G1–G10:
- G1: smooth-slab furnace, closed form.
- G2: emitter inside glass, which detects η² bugs.
- G3: rough reflection-only, by quadrature.
- G4: rough slab against an independent CPU Monte Carlo.
- G5: point light behind a smooth, rough or open pane; the smooth pane's shadow must be exactly zero.
- G6: mode-B caustic.
- G7: Principled mixtures.
- G8: Cornell box with glass objects, used for Gate 2 and the Gate 3 ladder.
- G9: IOR < 1 'bubble'.
- G10: coloured Glass node and Refraction node.
Also add planted biases B-η, B-shadow, B-tint, B-side and B-spur.

Extend the LUT buffer with the four Tier-2 glass tables: offsets 9248, 13344, 13600 and 17696, 17952 floats (71,808 B) in total, no new binding. Imported glTF glass defaults to Tier 2 because the importer leaves MULTI_GGX. Port glass_inv_E verbatim.

Loaders: map glTF transmission, IOR and volume exactly as Blender does. For volumes, use σ_a = (1−attenuationColor)/attenuationDistance, created only when thicknessFactor ≠ 0; defer this to phase G2 with a local inside/outside rule and warn in G1. Map USD opacity to Transmission Weight = 1 − opacity unless opacityThreshold > 0 or opacity comes from a texture's alpha. Flip triangle winding for negative-determinant transforms.

Interactive defaults: glass interfaces use up the total bounce budget, so use N ≥ 4 when glass is present. Cycles-style per-type bounce caps would need the suffix's per-type counts stored and re-checked in shifts, because the side at y_{k−1} or x_k can flip between glossy and transmission. Defer that. The denoiser should follow delta chains to the first non-delta vertex for its guide buffers.
risks: Mode B with rough glass cannot match Cycles exactly when NEE through a rough transmission lobe lands in the spurious region. Cycles weights that energy by w_C < 1 (power heuristic, light-tree pdf); we weight it by 1. The size is scene-dependent: about 0.1% of lobe energy at r = 0.2, a few % at r = 0.5, up to 60% at r = 1 grazing. It needs its own tolerance tier and a one-off measurement on G5b in mode B.

The plan's Mode A ≡ Mode B unit test fails on any scene with mirrors (r ≤ 0.00376) or smooth glass unless it is restricted. In mode A, smooth glass casts black shadows from every analytic light and mirrors never show lamps; users may read this as a bug, though Cycles mode A does the same.
A winding or negative-scale mismatch against Blender silently inverts η on whole objects. U-G8 plus a one-triangle GLB spike are needed.

Relaxed Metal math can flip reflect/refract near u_rt ≈ P_R and near the critical angle between pipelines. This is measure-small; classify such cases as floating-point boundary flips (gap-rc §8) and keep one shared glass_fresnel/bsdf_sample.

glass_inv_E does not match the current sampler in the TIR regime (cause unverified). Tier-2 inside behaviour is right only if the table is ported verbatim, and Tier-2 unit tests must expect the table values.
Smooth-shaded glass, which is common in GLBs, has the same Ng-rejection non-partition as gap-bsdf §8.2 for refraction. Flat shading is required for exact parity.

Delta glass forces full or late replay, so replay-queue occupancy and frame time on glass-heavy views may exceed the gap-perf budget (unverified; re-measure on G8). Caustic paths (delta vertex before the light) never reconnect, so ReSTIR gains little there.

Edge cases replicated but kept out of validation: rough glass with IOR within 1e-4 of 1 (sampled as delta, but NEE evaluates a rough spurious lobe) and glTF ior = 0 (degenerate after Cycles' max(ior, 1e-5)).

Volume absorption (KHR_materials_volume with thicknessFactor ≠ 0) is deferred. Phase G1 will not match Blender for such GLBs; phase G2 needs a local medium rule and cannot handle nested or overlapping meshes.

issues.plan_section: §3 passes 3-4 (suffix_refresh, temporal_*); §1 Kernels ('Suffix refresh is a separate pass'); §2 rule 8
issues.problem: Pass 3 says it will 'refresh prev-frame reservoirs under S_t, and canonical samples under S_{t-1} when needed' before temporal classification. There are four problems. (a) If pass 3 rewrites reservoir_prev (F or rcRadiance) in place, the stored route π_p(Y_p) = lum(F_p^st)/J_p no longer equals F_{t-1}(X_p), while π_p(X_c) comes from the exact E_{t-1}. That is the mixed evaluator whose partition of unity fails: B(r) = 1/(1+c_p) − r/(r+c_p), −4.3% for a 2× intensity step. It is exactly the Falcor bias that rule 8 forbids. (b) 'When needed' cannot be known in pass 3, because s is drawn later in temporal_resample. (c) The graph has no pass for the inverse shift T^{-1}(X_c): replay into q', reconnection and the S_{t-1} end term. It would be traced inside temporal_resample, which contradicts §1's rule that replay is a separate compacted indirect pass. (d) The write-back of a selected temporal sample (refreshed rcRadiance, jDen, light-index renumbering) is unspecified.
issues.fix:
Replace §3 step 3–4 with:
'3. temporal_classify: choose q' (see R8). Translate every stored light index of X_p (endpoint and suffix-cache lightIdx) with prevToCur; if any is −1, Y_p is undefined. Set c_p = min(20, c_prev). Do inline forward shifts for k=2 and class-L d=2. Ballot-append the rest to Q_f.
4. temporal_forward (indirect over Q_f): replay, reconnection, and end-term re-evaluation under S_t. The suffix refresh may be a separate pass, but it writes only a scratch buffer sufT[q]. It never writes reservoir_prev.
5. temporal_select: compute w̃_c and w̃_p, and draw s with the resampling RNG. If s = p, finalize W_Y with π_p(Y_p) = lum(F_p^st)/J_p read from the untouched reservoir_prev. If s = c, append q to Q_i.
6. temporal_inverse (indirect over Q_i): compute T^{-1}(X_c) under S_{t-1} (prev camera, prev jittered V-buffer, thr_{t-1}, lightsPrev, pmf_{t-1}, curToPrev). Re-evaluate the canonical end term under L_{t-1} from its suffix cache. Then finalize W_Y.
Invariants: reservoir_prev is read-only for the whole frame. The temporal output stores F_t(Y), rcRadiance and the end-term cache valid under S_t (I1), jDen ← J·jDen, all light indices in frame-t numbering, and c = c_c + c_p.'
Also change the §1 Kernels bullet to: 'Suffix/end-term refresh (forward under S_t, inverse under S_{t−1}) runs only on light- or pmf-change frames and writes scratch buffers only.'
issues.evidence: gap-temporal §3.3 (invariant I1; stored vs recomputed table), §3.4 proof step 1, §3.5(ii) B(r) table, §3.6 pseudo-code, §7 ('store the light index of the frame they were written in; translate on read'), §8.3 T1–T4 pass layout. gap-perf §2.4 (suffix as a separate pass, 2× suffix per moving-light frame). Plan lines 147–148, 262–266.

issues.plan_section: §2 rule 9 (Moving lights); §3 pass 0 (lightsChanged flags)
issues.problem: Rule 9 says the refresh runs 'only for samples on moved lights; an intensity or colour change is an analytic rescale'. That keys the refresh per light. But F contains 1/q = A/pmf(L) and the MIS weights ω1 and ω2, and these depend on the global power pmf. Any power edit, add or remove renormalizes pmf for every light. Two kinds of sample are then affected even when their own light is unchanged: every NEE-terminated sample (including emissive triangles), and every BSDF-hit-emitter ending (ω2 through p1 of the hit triangle). For all of them F_t ≠ F_{t−1}. With a per-light mask, I1 is violated. The forward shift then uses the wrong integrand, and the next frame's stored route is wrong. J_P only fixes the PSS reparametrization, not the integrand.
issues.fix: Append to rule 9: 'Refresh scope is per frame, not per light. If pmf_t ≠ pmf_{t−1} bitwise (any power or luminance edit, add or remove), every light-terminated sample gets its end term re-evaluated analytically, without rays. NEE ends: N_t = N_{t−1}·(Le_t/Le_{t−1})·(ω1_t/ω1_{t−1})·(q_{t−1}/q_t). BSDF-hit emitter ends, including emissive triangles in Mode A: ω2_t = p2/(M·p1_t + p2), with p1_t built from pmf_t. Shadow rays are needed only for samples whose own light moved, rotated or rescaled. Rebuild the alias table only when powers change, so pmf is bitwise stable otherwise. Test: ix-e at frame 14 must pass T6(b) on pixels lit only by the unchanged light B. Planted control N7: a per-light refresh mask must fail with the predicted sign (the unchanged light brightens when another brightens).'
issues.evidence: gap-temporal §5.1 (light-dependent terms: p1, ω1, ω2), §5.5 radiometric-rescale formula, §6 consistency check F_t(y)·J_P = ω_t f_t J_M / p^{t−1}, §7 table ('P_sel of all other lights changes'). gap-light §3.4–3.5 (F_NEE ∝ 1/q; ω2 uses p1 of the hit triangle).

issues.plan_section: §2 rule 4 (last bullet); §1 Reservoir ('plus the NEE light pdf')
issues.problem: 'Light vertices: J = 1 within a frame, and pmf_t/pmf_{t−1} across frames' is wrong or ambiguous in four ways. (i) For a BSDF-hit emitter used as rc vertex (case d, k = d), J = p^y_{d−1}(ω',ℓ)·G(y_{d−1}→z) / [p^x_{d−1}·G(x_{d−1}→z)], which is not 1. There is also never a pmf ratio, because that path has no light-selection dimension. (ii) J_P must multiply every NEE-terminated path (classes L, N1, D-NEE), not only those where the light vertex is the rc vertex. Omitting it gives the N2 bias. (iii) J = 1 holds only for area-uniform light-local (u,v) sampling with a shading-point-independent pmf. Porting Cycles' spherical-rectangle sampler silently breaks it. (iv) §1 caches 'the NEE light pdf', which invites reusing a p1 measured at a vertex the shift replaces (C2).
issues.fix:
Replace rule 4's last bullet with:
'Light-vertex factors.
(a) NEE-sampled light vertex (forced rc, k=d): J = 1 within a frame. This holds only because light points are sampled area-uniformly in light-local (u,v): rect uniform; disk/ellipse concentric; triangle b = (1−√u1, √u1(1−u2), √u1·u2). The pmf must also be shading-point independent. Any solid-angle light sampler requires J = p_A(z|y_{d−1}) / p_A(z|x_{d−1}).
(b) BSDF-hit emitter as rc vertex (case d): J = p^y_{d−1}(ω',ℓ_{d−1})·G(y_{d−1}→z) / cachedJden, with p_k := 1. No pmf factor, in any frame.
(c) Temporal: multiply by J_P = pmf_t(L)/pmf_{t−1}(L) for every NEE-terminated path (classes L, N1, D-NEE), wherever the light vertex sits relative to k. Never apply it to BSDF-hit endings.
(d) Delta lights and the sun: 1 (× J_P temporally), never t_x²/t_y².
(e) The only cacheable light pdf is p1 measured at the rc vertex x_{d−1} for case (c), within one frame. Cases (a) and (d) always recompute p1 at y_{d−1}.'

Enhanced Eq. 2 (p_k := 1 for k = d). gris-verify C2.

issues.plan_section: §2 rules 6 and 9 (inconsistency between the adopted gap-rc predicate and the gap-temporal refresh design)
issues.problem: The plan adopts gap-rc's predicate. Under it, the NEE candidate's pair (x_{d−2}, x_{d−1}) uses EV_NEE, whose invFP pdf is the BSDF pdf of the NEE direction. For forced NEE, O1 also tests (y_{d−2}, y_{d−1}) with EV_RECONNECT_NEE toward x_d. Both depend on the light point Φ_s(L,u,v). So k* and the class (L vs N1) change when a light moves or rotates, which contradicts gap-temporal §5.1 ('k is light-independent… the class of a path never changes under light edits') and its test §9.3-6 ('class invariance across light edits'). The rule-9 refresh and the suffix-cache classes rely on that invariance. If the forward shift or refresh trusts the stored k/class on light-change frames without re-running O1/O2 against Φ_t (and the inverse against Φ_{t−1}), the temporal shift is not bijective. The resulting bias concentrates on glossy x_{d−1} near moving lights. Mode-B BSDF_ANALYTIC pairs (x_{d−1}, z) have the same issue.
issues.fix:
Add to rule 6: 'k* is always evaluated in the destination frame's light state. Forward temporal shifts run O1/O2 with Φ_t(L,u,v) and the frame-t light normal. Inverse shifts use Φ_{t−1}. If k or the class would differ, the shift is undefined in both directions, using the same code. The refresh pass never relabels a reservoir's k or class.' Replace gap-temporal test §9.3-6 with: 'T defined ⇒ class and k preserved; report the class-change rate per light-change frame (T5 must still pass).'
Alternative, if light-independent classes are preferred: remove the EV_NEE pair from NEE candidates' pair lists and remove EV_RECONNECT_NEE from forced-NEE O1 (EvanLuo rule). Choose exactly one variant and code it only in rc.wgsl.
issues.evidence: gap-rc §0 items 3 and 6, §3.4 pair table (pair d−1 with EV_NEE), §3.5(g), §6.1 O1 ('For forced NEE it is EV_RECONNECT_NEE toward the shared light vertex x_d'), §3.5 item 1 (both variants unbiased only if applied identically). gap-temporal §5.1 and §9.3 test 6 (invariance claim).

issues.plan_section: §1 Materials ('VNDF sampling, rejecting samples below Ng exactly as Cycles does'; 'flat shading first'); §2 (missing rule)
issues.problem: The plan copies Cycles' asymmetry (samplers reject below Ng; eval does not). It never states that a shift re-evaluating a BSDF-sampled segment must apply the canonical sampler's support indicator. Examples are ω' at y_{k−1} with the copied lobe, and the stored ω_k at x_k under the new V. Without the indicator, p̂(ȳ) > 0 on paths the canonical path tree can never generate. That violates GRIS Def. 5.2, so ReSTIR adds energy that our own PT never integrates: bias against our PT, not only against Cycles. This happens for smooth shading, for normal maps (M7), and for refraction configurations with no valid microfacet. issues.problem: Rule 3 uses 'p1' for two different quantities. It is the solid-angle pdf inside ω1 = M·p1/(M·p1+p2), and it is also the factor in the UCW 'W^RIS·p1'. W^RIS is an area-measure (μ) UCW, so its factor must be the source density q in μ (P/A or P), not the solid-angle pdf. An implementer who multiplies by the solid-angle p1 introduces an r²/|cosθ_z| measure error, which is a bias. The rule also never states the BSDF-hit counterpart ω2 = p2/(M·p1+p2) with the same M. 'NEE source density in μ: q = P(L)/A_L (area light or emissive triangle, area-uniform) or q = P(L) (delta, sun).

issues.plan_section: §1 Materials ('Glass/transmission… spec from the glass gap report'); §8 pending; §2
issues.problem:
The plan gives no ReSTIR rules for transmission, and several are needed for unbiasedness.
(1) Cycles inverts η on backfacing hits and flips N and Ng. At a reconnection vertex x_k, or at y_{k−1}, η must come from the evaluating path's own V. A cached side or η from the base path is wrong for the offset.
(2) The joint pdf of glass sub-lobes is not a V-only q times a direction pdf. Cycles picks R vs T at the sampled H with P_R(H) = avg(R)/avg(R+T), and the refraction pdf carries the generalized-half-vector Jacobian η²|H·L|/(V·H + η·L·H)².
(3) Delta also covers refraction with |η−1| < 1e-4, which Cycles treats as singular, not just α_x·α_y ≤ 2e-10.
(4) The 2-bit lobe codes cannot hold R and T.
(5) The RNG layout must include the R/T decision (Cycles reuses the rescaled rand.z).
(6) Replay may flip R/T or hit TIR. That is allowed (PSS J = 1), but O3 must still hold.
(7) Reconnection through a medium needs ray origins offset to the side of travel.
(8) Gate 3 and the T3 case coverage contain no transmissive cases.

Add §2 rule 16 (glass) and require the glass spec to contain it:
'(a) Lobe codes are 3 bits: D, S, R_g, T_g, NEE, NONE (pathFlags bits 22–27). Delta iff α_x·α_y ≤ 2e-10, or, for T_g only, |η−1| < 1e-4.
(b) η and the N/Ng flip are never stored. Recompute them at every evaluation from the side of the evaluating V (backfacing ⇒ η = 1/ior). This applies at x_k with V^y = normalize(y_{k−1} − x_k) and at y_{k−1}.
(c) Joint pdfs (for J and the throughput):
  p(L, T_g|V) = q(G|V)·D_V(H)/(1+Λ(V))·|∂H/∂L|·(1 − P_R(H)), with H = −normalize(η·L + V), |∂H/∂L| = η²|H·L|/(V·H + η·L·H)² (Cycles: sqr(ior·inv_len_H)·|cos_HI·H·wo|).
  p(L, R_g|V) = q(G|V)·D_V(H)/(1+Λ(V))·1/(4|V·H|)·P_R(H).
  Marginal (MIS, footprints) = Σ over R_g and T_g, which are disjoint by side.
(d) Copying ℓ ∈ {R_g, T_g} fixes the interaction type. If V^y changes side so that ω_k violates it, the joint pdf is 0 and the shift is undefined, symmetrically.

(f) The fixed per-vertex RNG layout contains the R/T decision. Use Cycles' rescaled closure-selection dimension or a dedicated 4th slot, the same for every material.
(g) Replay may switch R/T or TIR; no special casing beyond O0 and O3.
(h) Every visibility test offsets both endpoints along sign(Ng·ω)·Ng of the travelled direction (R11).
(i) T3/T4 case list adds: rc at a rough-T x_k, rc after T at x_{k−1}, NEE-final rough glass, TIR during replay, and delta-glass chains (full replay).
Gate 3 adds rung 3.9: glass scenes (smooth, and rough with r ∈ {0.1, 0.3, 0.6}), our ReSTIR ≡ our PT.'

(b) caustics_reflective and caustics_refractive are not pinned. Under __CAUSTICS_TRICKS__, turning them off zeroes glass reflection/transmission tints after diffuse bounces, which is biased by design.

issues.problem: Replay queues use 1D dispatchWorkgroupsIndirect with 64-wide groups. That caps a queue at 65,535×64 = 4,194,240 items. When the indirect x exceeds maxComputeWorkgroupsPerDimension, the WebGPU spec makes the dispatch a no-op, and Dawn implements this with an injected validation pass that zeroes the args. Every pair in that queue is then silently skipped: its slots keep stale or zero values, the result darkens, and no error is raised. The cap is exceeded in configurations the gates use: 1080p with N=3 at replay fraction f_r > 0.67; ensemble E=64×256² with N=3 at f_r > 0.33; Offline unpaired, 6 neighbours × 2 directions at 1080p, at f_r > 0.17; Talbot-exact inverse over more than 4.19 M px; and T3's 10⁷ trials. The glass/mirror scene (vi) will have a high f_r. Three related problems: queue capacity per queue is unspecified (overflow also drops items silently); the gap-perf item encoding (p<<2)|s allows only 4 slots; and the ballot append must sit in subgroup-uniform control flow, so an early return for pixels outside the image is a compile error, or undefined behaviour if the diagnostic is switched off.

Add to §1 Kernels a normative sub-bullet 'Replay queues and indirect dispatch':
(a) Each `args` pass writes 2D indirect args: `g = ceil(count/64); args = (min(g,65535), ceil(g/65535), 1)`. Replay kernels compute `item = workgroup_index*64 + local_invocation_index` (`requires linear_indexing;`) and do nothing when `item >= count`. Every direct 1D dispatch (T3/T5/T7, reductions) uses the same split.
(b) One `queue` buffer holds a header {counter, capacity, overflowFlag} per queue at 256-B-aligned offsets, followed by item regions sized for the worst case of the largest configured mode: temporal-fwd P, temporal-inv P, spatial N_max·P. append() sets overflowFlag instead of writing past capacity. Every validation run reads the flags back and fails the gate if any is set.
(c) Item encoding is `(pixel<<4)|slot`: slot < 16, pixel < 2^28.
(d) append() is called unconditionally by every invocation, with `needs = inImage && valid && …`. There is no return or break before it, and `diagnostic(off, subgroup_uniformity)` is banned in src/core.
(e) Add GPU test T17: a 5 M-item queue (more than 4.19 M) is processed exactly once, checked by an item-id checksum. The 'queue occupancy' debug view shows count/capacity per queue.

It runs before selection, so 'canonical samples under S_{t−1} when needed' cannot be known at that point. 'Refresh prev-frame reservoirs under S_t', read as an in-place update, overwrites F_{t−1}(X_p), which is still needed as π_p(Y_p) = lum F_p^st / J_p (invariant I1). The plan does not allocate the suffixOut buffer at all.
issues.fix:
Replace §3 steps 3–4 with:
3. `suffix_refresh` (light-change frames only; one thread per pixel). Never write in place.
  (a) Forward: for each prev reservoir X_p[q'] whose endpoint light moved or changed, compute the refreshed suffix radiance under S_t and write it to `suffixOut.fwd[q']`.
  (b) Inverse: for each canonical X_c[q] whose endpoint light changed, compute its suffix radiance under S_{t−1} (via curToPrev, lightsPrev, pmf_{t−1}) and write it to `suffixOut.inv[q]`. The predicate is 'endpoint light changed', not 'canonical selected'.
  suffixOut is 2×16 B/px in validation (f32 rgb + flags) and 2×8 B/px in production. It is bound rw here and ro in T1, T2 and T4.
4. Temporal:
  T1 `temporal_classify`: back-projection, G-buffer test, 3×3 search, light-id translation, and the inline reconnection-only forward shift (rc = x2, class L). Writes the temporal fwd slot {F_t(Y_p), J_p, status} and appends forward replays to Q_f.
  → args
  T2 `temporal_fwd_replay` (indirect): replay + reconnect under S_t, reading suffixOut.fwd, and writes the fwd slot.
  T3 `temporal_select`: computes w̃_c and w̃_p and selects with the resampling RNG. If s = p, it finalizes W_Y from the stored π_p and writes reservoir_cur. If s = c, it writes {Σw̃, π_c, c_p} to the temporal select plane and appends q to Q_i.
  → args
  T4 `temporal_inv_replay` (indirect): T⁻¹(X_c) with the previous camera, previous jittered V-buffer, thr_{t−1}, lightsPrev, pmf_{t−1} and suffixOut.inv, then finalizes W_Y in reservoir_cur.
  In Talbot-exact debug mode, T3 enqueues every valid pixel into Q_i.
issues.evidence: gap-temporal §3.3 (the stored route for π_p(Y_p) and invariant I1), §3.6 pseudo-code (the inverse shift only when s = c), §8.3 (the T1–T4 layout with Q_f/Q_i and 'replay + reconnection + refresh'). gap-perf §4.2 B9 suffixOut '2 × 8 B/px (fwd and inv)' and §2.4 (keep the suffix work in a separate pass). issues.plan_section: §1 Device (relaxed math) and Kernels (compile-time rules); §2 rule 6; §5 M4 (T2/T3); §7 Gate 0
issues.problem: Initial sampling, replay, shift and inverse evaluation are separate pipelines. Chrome compiles MSL with fp math_mode(relaxed): FMA contraction was measured, and reassociation and reciprocal-division are allowed. So the same WGSL can yield different last-ulp values for ray origins, footprints and pdfs in different pipelines. Near a threshold, a predicate can then flip, or a replayed ray can hit the neighbouring triangle at an edge. Gate 0 requires 'zero invertibility logic violations', but the plan never says how FP-boundary flips (expected rate about 1e-7 to 1e-6, so a few in 10⁷ T3 trials) are told apart from logic bugs. It also omits the single-engine validation build, the only configuration in which the FP class is exactly 0. The plan's ban on a single traversal call site (39% slower) contradicts that build unless the ban is limited to production. Further gaps: whether strictMath has any effect on macOS 26.6 is unverified. The V-buffer bary precision in validation is unstated; a quantized x1 would drift off the camera ray.
issues.fix:
Add to §2 rule 6: 'FP-boundary vs logic violations.'
- Every predicate and replay decision records a margin: log2(fp/thr) per pair, and the replayed hit's distance to the nearest triangle edge.
- T2/T3 classify a mismatch as FP-BOUNDARY iff |margin| < 2^-16 or the hit lies within 1e-6 of an edge; otherwise it is LOGIC.
- Gate 0 becomes: LOGIC = 0; FP-BOUNDARY ≤ 1e-5 per round trip in the production pipelines; and FP-BOUNDARY = 0 in a 'single-engine' validation build.
- The single-engine build is one compute pipeline that runs initial sampling, prefix replay, reconnection and inverse evaluation through a runtime `mode` uniform. It has exactly one call site each of traverse(), vertexFromIds(), offsetRay(), rcPairTest(), bsdfEvalPdf() and bsdfSample(). The 39% runtime cost applies only to this build; production keeps per-stage pipelines, and the §1 ban on a single traversal site is scoped to production.

Add to §1 Device:
- The V-buffer stores bary as f32 bits in validation. unorm16 is allowed only in the 96 B layout, and there it is quantized before first use.
- All denominators are guarded with integer-bit tests before dividing. Never use min/max or NaN propagation to sanitize values.
- T1 cross-lane equality is asserted bitwise only for integer outputs (RNG words, IDs).

Add to M0: probe FMA/NaN folding with and without `strictMath:true` (requires `--enable-webgpu-developer-features`) on macOS 26.6. Only if strictMath changes the probe, add an A/B run of T2–T6 with strictMath on.
issues.evidence: gap-rc §8.1 (FMA measured, no `precise` qualifier in WGSL), §8.2 (flip magnitude ~1e-7 to 1e-6), §8.3 item 7 ('single path engine … T3's FP-class count must be exactly 0'), §9 FP-BOUNDARY row ('Must be exactly 0 in the single-pipeline validation build'), open question 7 (strictMath on macOS 26 unverified). webgpu-platform §8.1 (pragma relaxed on macOS 15+; measured FMA). gap-perf §2.8 (state machine 39% slower). validation-harness T2 and §5.6(b). sw_vers on this machine: 26.6.2.

issues.plan_section: §1 Reservoir (validation layout); §3 Modes; §7 Gate 3 ladder (ensemble R ≥ 256, dynamic ix-a…e)
issues.problem: The Gate 3 ladder relies on ensemble runs, but the plan defines no ensemble mode: no member layout, no member isolation for spatial and paired partners or for temporal reprojection, no reduction across members, and no memory budget. The only budget available (gap-perf, 1.31 GB for E=64×256²) assumed 64 B reservoirs. The plan's validation layout (uncompressed f32 core plus the f32 suffix cache) is 8 SoA planes = 128 B, and f32 slots are 32 B. Per pixel that gives about 540 B: reservoirs 2×128, paired slots 3×32, temporal slot plus select state 48, queues 20, V-buffer cur/prev 2×32, motion 8, suffixOut 32, colour 16. At E=64×256² (4.19 M px) that is about 2.26 GB, with a 1.07 GB reservoir arena and about 300–500 ms of GPU per ensemble frame. There is a pairing problem too: if the atlas shares one per-frame pairing transform and pairs across member borders, members are no longer independent runs.
issues.fix:
Add §3 'Ensemble mode (validation only)':
- E members are tiled as an atlas of 256² tiles. Default E = 16 (4×4 atlas = 1024², about 566 MB); E = 64 (2048², about 2.3 GB) is allowed only after the M0 allocation probe succeeds. All allocations happen inside pushErrorScope('out-of-memory').
- The RNG seed includes the member id. All members share the camera and light script; the primary pass maps an atlas pixel to its member-local pixel.
- Spatial acceptance A(p,q) includes `member(p)==member(q)`, which is symmetric. Pairing lookups use member-local coordinates with a per-member dihedral transform and offset, taken from a uniform array indexed by member id and derived from (frameSeed, memberId). Temporal back-projection stays inside the member.
- A reduction pass (one thread per member-local pixel) loops over the E members and writes per-frame (Σx, Σx²) in f32. These are flushed to f64 on the CPU (2 MB per frame at 256²).
- Each ensemble frame is submitted per pass family, so no submit exceeds the §5 budget (see WGPU-5).
- R = 256 is 16 sequential batches of E = 16.
- Add the resulting memory table (per-B/px as above) to §1 Reservoir.
issues.evidence: gap-perf §5.3 (312 B/px at 64 B reservoirs → 1.31 GB; 537 MB reservoir buffer; 230–280 ms per frame; split submits). validation-harness §3.6 (ensemble design: 'Spatial neighbors are clamped inside the member's viewport', Welford on GPU, f64 flush). gap-temporal §5.6 (+32 B suffix cache). gap-rc §8.3 item 5 (lossless rc data in validation). Plan §1 Reservoir: 'Validation: the same fields uncompressed, all f32'. hw.memsize on this Mac = 48 GB, so this is feasible but must be budgeted.

issues.plan_section: §3 Modes (Offline, PT); §5 M0/M2 (harness, PT batches); §7 automated tests
issues.problem: No per-submit GPU-time budget, checkpointing, or device-loss resume is specified for long runs. Offline mode runs 32 initial path trees per pixel, about 28 ns/px each: roughly 1.9 s in one dispatch at 1080p and 0.23 s at 512². A 4096-spp PT batch at 512² is 1.07e9 paths, which at the measured Sponza rate of about 27 Mpaths/s is about 40 s if submitted as one batch. The stated 262,144-spp reference at 512² is about 43 min per Sponza-class configuration. The platform guidance is to keep each submit at or below 100–200 ms, and macOS or Chrome can lose the device on long command buffers. Streaming RIS split across dispatches needs persisted running state (Σw), which is not in the reservoir. Running Blender (Metal) at the same time as Chrome GPU jobs adds contention and timeout risk and invalidates any timing.
issues.fix:
Add §7 'Submit budget and checkpointing' (normative):
1. No queue.submit may exceed 100 ms of GPU time. This is measured with timestamps and controlled by adapting the work per submit.
2. PT reference: each 4096-spp batch is split into sub-submits of k spp (start k = 16 at 512², adapt from timing) that accumulate into the f32 batch buffer. Every completed batch is read back and POSTed immediately; meta.json lists the completed batches.
3. Offline mode: the 32 initial path trees run as ⌈32/c⌉ dispatches of c candidates. {Σw, selected sample} persists in the reservoir (validation plane P4.w) and is finalized as W = Σw/p̂ in a last step. Each spatial round is its own submit.
4. 1080p progressive and validation frames submit per pass family.
5. The harness drives frames with `await device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone()`, never requestAnimationFrame.
6. On device.lost: call requestAdapter() and requestDevice() again, rebuild from the CPU copies, and resume at the first incomplete batch or ensemble run. After 3 losses on one job, fail the gate and report the loss reason.
7. Blender reference jobs and Chrome GPU jobs never run concurrently.

Add to M0: record our PT samples per second at 512² for the Cornell box and Sponza, and derive each Gate 2/3 spp and run budget from the MDB target before M2.
issues.evidence: webgpu-platform §7 ('Keep each submit ≲ 100–200 ms'; C2 tiles dispatches; device.lost needs a new adapter) and §4.1 (77.3 ms per 1080p 3-bounce+NEE frame ≈ 26.8 Mpaths/s). reference-code §3.3 (watchdog). validation-harness §5.6 (command-buffer duration, f32 per-batch then f64) and §3.2 (≥ 262,144 spp default). gap-perf §2.5 (initial path tree about 25.7 ms at 720p ≈ 28 ns/px). reference-code §1.10 (Offline preset: 32 candidates).

issues.plan_section: §1 Textures; §5 M1 (bucket textures), M7 (KTX2, end-to-end stock GLB vs Cycles)
issues.problem: Square power-of-two bucketing requires resampling any texture whose size is not a class size, which changes the integrand. Every textured Cycles comparison (the M7 end-to-end GLB, V2 sweeps with textures) is then biased by construction. The padding alternative breaks hardware wrap. Cycles on Metal samples the original-resolution byte texture with a hardware linear sampler (repeat, clamp_to_edge, clamp_to_zero or mirrored_repeat), no mips, then un-associates alpha, then decodes sRGB. Matching that exactly needs native-size textures and the same sampler address mode. Other unspecified details: createImageBitmap by default applies colour-space conversion and premultiplication; 16-bit, HDR and KTX2/BC7 sources cannot match Cycles' decode; interactive mips must be built in linear space; there is no texture memory budget (200 textures at 2048² is about 4.5 GB); and CLIP (clamp-to-zero) has no WebGPU address mode.
issues.fix:
Replace the §1 Textures bullets with:

Validation mode (every Cycles comparison):
- No resampling. One texture_2d_array per distinct (w,h) in the scene, at most 16 in validation scenes.
- Each texture's material record holds {array, layer, uvSet, wrap}. Sampling uses a hardware linear sampler with the matching address mode (repeat, clamp-to-edge or mirror-repeat), textureSampleLevel at LOD 0, on rgba8unorm, then Cycles' order: un-associate alpha when the texture has non-constant alpha (svm/image.h), then sRGB→linear for colour textures. CLIP is done in the shader (return 0 outside [0,1]).
- Validation assets are 8-bit PNG or JPEG only. 16-bit, HDR, KTX2 and BC7 are rejected or flagged 'interactive-only'.

Interactive mode:
- Square size classes (256–2048) with resampling are allowed, plus ray-cone LOD. Mips are generated in linear space (decode → filter → encode).

Both modes:
- Decode in the Worker with `createImageBitmap(blob,{colorSpaceConversion:'none', premultiplyAlpha:'none'})`, and upload with `copyExternalImageToTexture(…,{premultipliedAlpha:false})`.
- Allocate arrays inside pushErrorScope('out-of-memory') against a 2 GB texture budget. On failure, interactive mode steps the largest class down.
issues.evidence: Cycles 5.1.2 kernel/device/metal/compat.h:387-395 (metal_samplers: repeat, clamp_to_edge, clamp_to_zero, mirrored_repeat × nearest/linear). device/metal/context_begin.h:42 (tex.sample with the hardware sampler). device/gpu/image.h:86-100 (no mip path). svm/image.h:28-38 (ALPHA_UNASSOCIATE, then color_srgb_to_linear). critique X6. scene-io §3.2 ('no mip-mapping in Cycles'; wrap mapping; 'resample … keep a per-layer UV scale if padding'). webgpu-platform §3.2 (square resampling recommendation; 4.5 GB example).

issues.plan_section: §5 M4 (spatial reuse with random neighbours); §3 step 5 and Modes (Offline 3 rounds × 6 neighbours); §1 Reservoir (8-bit M)
issues.problem: M4 prescribes random-neighbour, unpaired pairwise MIS, but §3, the binding plan and the slot layout describe only the paired structure, where each pixel shifts its own path into each partner and each shift is computed once per pair. Unpaired reuse needs two shifts per neighbour (neighbour→centre and centre→neighbour), 2N slots, queue items with a direction bit, and a different spatial_shift kernel. That is a second kernel family that is neither specified nor budgeted, and it is superseded in M6. Offline mode (6 unpaired neighbours × 2 directions) also multiplies queue size (see WGPU-1). With 3 rounds, the uncapped spatial confidence reaches 7³ = 343, which overflows the 8-bit M of the production layout.
issues.fix:
Change M4 to: 'Spatial reuse uses the paired pass structure from the start (pair_accept → args → spatial_replay_reconnect → spatial_shift → spatial_resample, one slot per partner). In M4 the partner maps are CPU-generated random involutions within radius r (a fresh perfect matching per frame and round, uploaded as rg8sint textures). M6 swaps them for the σ=16 pairing textures without changing any kernel.'

Change Offline mode to: '32 candidates, 3 rounds × N=6 paired partner maps (6 textures, fresh transforms each round), rounds ping-pong A→B→A→B, validation layout only (f32 confidence; c ≤ 343 does not fit 8-bit M).'

Add to §1 Reservoir: '8-bit M is legal only when c_max = (c_cap+1)·(1+N)^rounds ≤ 255; otherwise the validation layout is required.'

issues.plan_section: §1 Bindings; §3 pass graph
issues.problem: The plan's claim of '≤ 8 of 10 storage buffers' comes from gap-perf's graph, which lacks T3/T4, suffixOut, the Cycles LUTs, a full-frame debug output and the ensemble reduction. Under an explicit shared G0 layout, lightTiles (B4) counts against every pass. Adding these pushes some passes to 9–10 with no recorded tally. The write-set rule is stated only for buffers, but the V-buffer, thr and motion textures swap roles cur↔prev, and a texture that is written as storage cannot also be sampled in the same pass. Presenting to the canvas is also unspecified: a compute write needs bgra8unorm-storage, which is not in the feature list.
issues.fix:
Replace the §1 Bindings bullet with a per-pass table (extending gap-perf §4.4) and these rules:
- Put the LUTs (36,992 B), alias/pmf cur and prev, id maps and lights cur and prev into `records` (B3).
- Move `lightTiles` (B4) out of the shared G0 into the G1 of `presample_lights` (rw) and `initial` (ro) only.
- The resulting maximum is T4 = bvh, tris, records (3) + reservoirs rw, slots rw, queue ro, suffixOut ro (4) + probe (1) = 8.
- Textures follow the same write-set rule as buffers. cur/prev V-buffer, thr and motion roles swap by choosing between 2 prebuilt bind-group variants, never by binding one texture as both storage and sampled.
- Present and upscale through a fullscreen render pass that samples `color`. If a compute write to the canvas is ever used, add `bgra8unorm-storage` to the required features.

issues.plan_section: §1 Geometry and BVH; §5 M1 (traversal guards, T12)
issues.problem: The limits of the BVH encoding and the failure modes of traversal are not tied to validation. The Aila–Laine leaf reference allows at most 127 triangles per leaf and firstTri < 2^24 (16.7 M triangles). The 32-entry private stack (and the CWBVH group stack) silently drops pushes on overflow, and an iteration-cap exit returns a miss. Both are missed occluders, which cause light leaks, which bias the result. Under FMA contraction, Möller–Trumbore and even Woop are not watertight on shared edges unless edge functions are evaluated in a canonical order. That matters for T12, the glass scene (vi) and the contact-geometry scene (xi). Degenerate triangles produce Inf or NaN in 1/a.
issues.fix:
Add to §1 Geometry and BVH:
(a) The loader rejects scenes with more than 2^24 triangles (or the leaf encoding is widened), and leaves are capped at 3–4 triangles.
(b) The SAH builder caps depth at 30 by forcing a median split or a leaf beyond that depth. The traversal counts stack overflows and iteration-cap exits (cap 1<<16) in the probe buffer, and every validation run fails if either count is non-zero.
(c) Zero-area and non-finite triangles are dropped at flatten time and logged; primIds stay stable.
(d) T12 watertightness and scenes (vi) and (xi) run the Woop intersector. Its triangle record stores v0, v1, v2 plus global vertex ids, and edge functions are evaluated in canonical global-vertex order so that shared edges contract identically.
issues.evidence: webgpu-platform §4.2 (leaf ≤ 127, 16.7 M triangles), §4.3 notes (tinybvh 'silently drops pushes'; loop guard; watchdog on runaway loops), §8.2 (FMA can make a shared edge evaluate differently; canonical endpoint order). gap-perf §10.2 (the CWBVH stack silently drops pushes).

issues.plan_section: §1 Kernels (createComputePipelineAsync, 6 pipelines: 0.7 s; override rule)
issues.problem: The plan has several code-shape axes: reservoir layout (validation or production), BSDF (V1, V2+glass, Tier 2), BVH2 or CWBVH, MT or Woop, BVH debug counters, and single-engine or per-stage. Each has about 20 pipelines: primary, presample, initial, refresh, T1–T4, args, pair_accept, spatial replay/shift/resample, dupmap, accumulate, SVGF×3, resolve, debug_view, reduce. Each distinct override or #define set is a full Tint→MSL→Metal compile of 0.2–0.9 s, with a material-library cost of 70–160 ms per inlined copy. The '6 pipelines: 0.7 s' figure understates startup, and the UI toggles (PT/ReSTIR, validation layout, V1/V2) would compile on demand with nothing in the plan to handle the stall.
issues.fix:
Add to §1 Kernels a pipeline-variant table listing the axes above, and state:
- Only the active variant is compiled at startup, in parallel (about 2–4 s).
- Other variants compile lazily on toggle behind a progress indicator, cached in a Map keyed by the variant hash, and never inside the frame loop.
- debugMode is a uniform. Only BVH instrumentation is an override.
- BSDF-bearing kernels route every eval through one call site (the E2e pattern, −17% compile time).
- Validation runs pre-compile their single variant before the timed loop.

issues.plan_section: §5 M2 compare.py; §7 Gates 1-3 decision rules
issues.problem:
The decision rules have four statistical flaws.

(a) No suite-level error control. Each scene/config/gate/channel uses Šidák α=0.01 plus χ²_red, KS and mean-t checks. With ≈50-100 units per `npm run validate`, P(at least one false failure) is about 40-60%. With 'stop at first failure' and M8 CI, this makes the gates flaky, and people will learn to ignore failures.

(b) Relative δ on dark or zero tiles (black background in C0a, falloff tails in C0c, outside the spot cone) makes TOST fail or produces NaN (0/0).

(c) Luminance-only tests miss chromatic bugs (e.g., the Enhanced RGB shading weights), and ReSTIR's p̂ is luminance.

(d) The planted controls (light ×1.01, dropped Jacobian) are 2-5× larger than the Stage-B δ of 0.2%, so they do not show that the harness can certify 0.2%. There is also no A/A test for ReSTIR ensembles, which is where correlation handling can go wrong.

'(1) Suite FWER: each run declares n_units = scenes × configs × gates × {Y, R, G, B}. Every rejection-type test uses α_u = 1 − 0.99^{1/n_units}. A failed unit is re-run once with a disjoint seed range, and the gate fails only if the re-run also fails at α_u. Gate 1 runs the whole suite A/A 20 times and requires ≤ 1 suite-level false alarm.'
